plan.title: Liver drug-treatment modules via STRING prior network (n=6)
plan.analytical_narrative:
The research question asks which co-expression modules the 12,000 genes form across the 6 liver samples (3 drug-treated vs 3 control, unpaired, single batch, gene-level Salmon counts in counts.csv with the matching metadata.csv condition column) and which of those modules track treatment. The binding constraint is the cohort size: 6 samples. A correlation coefficient estimated from 6 observations has a standard error large enough that a de novo WGCNA correlation network would recover modules of correlation noise rather than shared regulation, and the knowledge service flags this design explicitly (R-0140: fewer than 15 samples, do not build the network from the expression alone). The plan therefore does NOT estimate the module structure from these 6 samples. It takes the module structure from a prior: the STRING v12.0 human functional association network staged in the reference store, thresholded at the conventional high-confidence cut combined_score >= 700, restricted to the genes that survive the low-count filter, and partitioned into modules by community detection on that fixed graph. The samples are then used only to score each prior module per sample and to describe how the scores separate treated from control — a descriptive read-out on 3 vs 3, not an inferential claim.

Order: T1S1 QC of the sample structure on the blind VST matrix (PCA on the 500 most variable genes, sample distance heatmap, library sizes) so the reader can see whether the two conditions separate at all before any module is scored. T1S2 applies the standard pre-filter (>=10 counts in at least 3 samples, the smallest group size) and produces the VST matrix that the scoring uses; median-of-ratios size factors are computed inside DESeq2 and the counts are never pre-scaled. T3S3 builds the prior-network modules and places the filtered genes on them. T3S4 scores each module per sample from the VST matrix (first principal component of the module's genes, sign-fixed to the mean gene, plus the mean z-score as a robustness check) and ranks the modules by the separation between treated and control, reporting an unadjusted Wilcoxon or t statistic alongside the BH-adjusted values with the explicit statement that with 3 vs 3 the smallest attainable rank-test p-value is 0.1 and nothing here can reach significance. T1S3 assembles the report with the sample count stated beside every module, the gene-to-module table, the module scores, and the reproducibility record.

What this plan will not deliver, stated up front: a data-driven module structure specific to this liver drug-treatment experiment, and any statistically supported claim that a module responds to treatment. Both require more samples. If the intent is genuinely a de novo co-expression network, the honest answer is a cohort of 15-20 or more samples; the modules reported here are prior knowledge annotated with this experiment's direction of change.

keep genes with >=10 counts in at least smallest group size samples
median-of-ratios size factors inside DESeq2 model
STRING prior protein-protein association network as module structure; descriptive only, no de novo WGCNA correlation network
co-expression report with sample count, module sizes, gene-module table, eigengene-condition association, reproducibility record

steps.name: Report
steps.question: What are the prior-network modules over the expressed liver genes, which of them separate the 3 drug-treated from the 3 control samples, and what can and cannot be concluded from 6 samples?
steps.description: Assemble a single report from T1S1, T1S2, T3S3 and T3S4. Lead with the limitation: 6 samples (3 drug-treated, 3 control) is below the ~15-sample floor at which gene-gene correlations become stable, so the module structure was taken from a prior human functional association network and was not learned from this dataset; a de novo co-expression network was deliberately not built and the reason is stated. Then report: sample count and gene count entering the network, the network source and version, the edge confidence cut, the identifier mapping rate, the module count with sizes and hub genes, the full gene-to-module table, the per-sample module scores, and the module-versus-condition differences with unadjusted and BH-adjusted p-values. State plainly that a module is a group of associated genes and not a proven pathway, and that a module-condition association is descriptive in this cohort. Close with the concrete requirement for a de novo answer: a cohort of at least 15-20 samples. Include the reproducibility record: sessionInfo, package versions, the random seed used for community detection, and the STRING release version.
steps.context: Final deliverable for the co-expression question on the liver drug-treatment dataset.

flags.message: If the cohort holds at most two groups of at most 7 samples, the total is below 15 samples, and a correlation across so few samples is unstable. Do not build a co-expression network from the expression alone on such a cohort, because the modules would reflect the noise of the correlations and not a shared regulation. State the sample count and the reason in the plan. Then either take a prior network, for example the STRING protein-protein associations of the reference store, as the structure and place the genes of interest on it, or stop and ask for a cohort of at least 15 to 20 samples.
